headline: Turner's two-run single in the ninth walks off Giants
recap: Trailing 3-2 entering the bottom of the ninth, the Phillies beat the San Francisco Giants 4-3 at Citizens Bank Park. Bryson Stott was hit by a pitch to open the inning and Jake Cave flew out, then Brandon Marsh singled to put runners on first and third. Kyle Schwarber was intentionally walked to load the bases, and Marsh stole second during that at-bat. Trea Turner then lined a single to right field off closer Camilo Doval, the ball deflecting off Doval's glove, scoring Stott and Marsh to end the game.

Taijuan Walker started for the Phillies and allowed three runs, two earned, on six hits over five innings with seven strikeouts and two walks. Giants starter Kyle Harrison worked 3 1/3 innings, also charged with two earned runs. Bryce Harper opened the scoring for Philadelphia with a two-run homer, his 11th of the season, in the bottom of the first that also drove in Schwarber and put the Phillies ahead 2-1.

San Francisco had taken a 1-0 lead in the top of the first when Wilmer Flores grounded into a force out that scored LaMonte Wade Jr., then went back ahead 3-2 in the top of the fifth on Joc Pederson's two-run double that scored Thairo Estrada and Flores. Craig Kimbrel pitched a scoreless ninth to earn the win, and Doval took the loss after blowing the save.
